Fixed effects, random effects and variance components

Source: R/hier_methods.R
countreg_hier-effects.Rd

fixef() returns the fixed coefficients of the mean, ranef() the conditional modes of the random effects (one data frame per grouping factor, with their posterior covariances in the attribute "postVar"), and VarCorr() the estimated covariance matrices of the random effects.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'countreg_hier'
fixef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'countreg_hier'
ranef(object, condVar = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'countreg_hier'
VarCorr(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'VarCorr.countreg_hier'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

object

a countreg_hier() fit.

...

unused.

condVar

include the posterior covariances.

x

a VarCorr() result.

digits

number of significant digits to print.

Value

fixef(): a named vector. ranef(): a named list of data frames. VarCorr(): a named list of covariance matrices with attributes "stddev" and "correlation".

Examples

# \donttest{
data("washington_roads")
h <- countreg_hier(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + offset(lnlength) + (1 | ID),
                   data = washington_roads, family = "POISSON")
fixef(h)
#> (Intercept)      lnaadt 
#>   -9.445363    1.148339 
head(ranef(h)$ID)
#>   (Intercept)
#> 1  -0.4459850
#> 2   0.4177328
#> 3  -0.4282198
#> 4   0.5740780
#> 5  -0.4678016
#> 6   0.1352786
VarCorr(h)
#>  Groups Name        Variance Std.Dev.
#>  ID     (Intercept) 0.4658   0.6825  
# }
